title: Human Resources and Office Administration Manager
description:
About the company A leading global technology, defence and engineering group with diverse business interests across Aerospace, Defence & Public Security, Urban Solutions & Satcom etc., The company has recently established its subsidiary operations in India and is focused on building and expanding its presence across multiple business lines in the Indian market. This offers an exciting opportunity to be part of its growth journey and contribute to developing its India operations as the business scales. About the Role The HR Manager & Office Assistant is a dual-function role responsible for managing the full spectrum of Human Resources activities while providing comprehensive administrative and office support. This position plays a critical role in ensuring effective people management, compliance with employment legislation, smooth office operations, and a professional, well-organized working environment. The role combines strategic HR leadership with hands-on office administration and coordination. Human Resources Management Responsibilities Workforce Planning & HR Advisory Support management in workforce planning, manpower forecasting, budgeting and costs tracking succession planning and organizational structuring. Provide guidance to management and employees on HR policies, ethical practices, and governance standards. Recruitment & Onboarding Manage the full recruitment lifecycle, including manpower requisitions, job postings, rsum screening, interviews, and offer management. Manage onboarding formalities for new hires, including, background checks (where required), pre-employment medical check-up, work setup, orientation and induction programmes. Manage recruitment of outsourced staff for projects as required. Maintain accurate and up-to-date employee records and employment contracts. Employee Relations & Engagement Serve as the primary point of contact for all HR-related employee enquiries. Handle employee grievances, disciplinary matters, and conflict resolution in a professional and confidential manner. Support and promote employee engagement initiatives to foster a positive and inclusive workplace culture. Performance Management Administer the performance management framework, including goal setting, performance reviews, and feedback cycles. Support managers in the implementation of performance improvement plans (PIPs) and employee development initiatives. Track and analyse performance outcomes to support talent retention and succession planning. Compensation & Benefits Administration Coordinate with the external payroll vendor to ensure accurate and timely payroll processing. Prepare and validate payroll input data (e.g., attendance, leaves, new hires, exits, salary changes, allowances, claims). Review payroll outputs from the vendor, including payslips, reports, and statutory calculations for accuracy. Liaise with Finance and the vendor to resolve payroll discrepancies or issues. Manage payroll documentation and maintain proper records Respond to employee payroll queries and provide clarifications on payslips, deductions, and benefits. Administer employee benefits, including leave management, insurances, claims, and statutory contributions. Compliance & HR Governance Develop, implement, and maintain HR policies and procedures in compliance with applicable labour laws, regulations, and internal standards. Support internal and external audits by maintaining proper documentation and ensuring audit readiness. Manage statutory compliance requirements, including filings, reporting, and record-keeping. Identify compliance risks and recommend corrective actions to mitigate potential issues. Drive awareness and training on compliance, code of conduct, and corporate governance requirements. Training & Development Identify employee training needs and coordinate internal or external training programmes. Maintain training records and support skills development, career progression, and succession planning initiatives. Manage training budgets and track learning participation and outcomes. Office Assistant / Administrative Responsibilities Office Administration & Operations Oversee daily office operations to ensure an efficient, organised, and professional working environment. Manage office supplies, inventory, stationery, and pantry stock. Coordinate office maintenance and liaise with vendors and service providers (cleaning, IT support, repairs, etc.). Process invoices and coordinate submissions for payment. Liaise with HR and administrative vendors (e.g. payroll providers, outsourced services, PRO services). Organise company events, staff activities, and internal functions. Prepare official correspondence, letters, and internal memos. Provide administrative support and handle ad hoc duties as required. Documentation Records & Reporting Maintain systematic filing and record-keeping systems for HR and general office documentation (both physical and electronic). Handle incoming and outgoing correspondence, emails, and courier services. Prepare reports, letters, and documentation in support of management and operational needsPrepare HR-related reports and submissions for management, HR, Finance, General Manager, and parent office as required Maintain all company and employee records with strict confidentiality. Front Desk & Coordination Act as the first point of contact for visitors, vendors, and external partners. Support meeting coordination, meeting room bookings, and internal events. Provide administrative and coordination support to management and other departments as required. Travel & Logistics Support Coordinate travel arrangements, accommodations, and expense documentation for staff and management. Assist in organising office events, staff functions, and company activities. Support visa applications and the renewal of licenses and statutory certificates. Required Qualifications & Experience Bachelors degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related discipline. Minimum 57 years of relevant experience in Human Resources, with hands-on exposure to office administration or office management. Strong working knowledge of employment laws and HR practices. Demonstrated experience in payroll management, recruitment, employee relations, and office administration. Required Skills & Competencies Strong interpersonal, communication, and stakeholder management skills. High level of confidentiality, integrity, and professionalism. Excellent organisational, coordination, and time-management abilities. Ability to multitask effectively and manage dual responsibilities independently. Proficiency in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and HR systems. Strong attention to detail with a problem-solving mindset. Ability to work with minimal supervision. Adaptable, proactive, and service-oriented attitude.

title: Consultant - Learning & Development
description:
Qualifications As a Full-Time LD Consultant - Category Management, you will serve as an embedded capability specialist and instructional architect within the Instamart business unit. You will work side-by-side with Category Directors, VPs, and HR Business Partners (HRBPs) to translate business strategies into actionable, high-impact learning frameworks. Your principal mission is to drastically reduce Time-to-Productivity (TTP) for new hires across Category Manager (CM), Associate Category Manager (ACM), and Buyer roles, while continuously upskilling existing teams on complex commercial topics such as Joint Business Planning (JBP), contribution margin enhancement, stockout mitigation, and tail-end assortment rationalization. Detailed Responsibilities Key Deliverables 1. Strategic Training Needs Analysis (TNA) Competency Mapping Partner directly with Category VPs, Senior Category Managers, and HR leadership to map operational skill gaps across distinct verticals (Fresh Produce, FMCG, Non-Food, Electronics, and Seasonal Categories). Conduct ongoing job-task and competency gap analyses to establish clear proficiency standards for Category Leads, CMs, ACMs, and Category Support Associates. Align training objectives directly with key business outcome metrics including Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), Contribution Margin, Inventory Turnover Ratio, Fill Rates, and Shrinkage/Wastage metrics. 2. Curriculum Architecture Functional Playbook Development Design, build, and continuously refine functional learning playbooks, interactive micro-learning modules, digital reference guides, and real-world case simulations tailored for rapid execution. Develop comprehensive training tracks covering core quick-commerce capabilities: PL Commercial Management: Unit economics, gross margin optimization, contribution margin calculation, pricing strategies, markdown mechanics, and promotion ROI analysis. Supply Chain Inventory Dynamics: Dark store fill rates, out-of-stock (OOS) reduction, safety stock calculation, shrinkage/wastage control, and demand forecasting models. Vendor Management Commercial Negotiations: Joint Business Planning (JBP), vendor terms negotiation (margins, payment terms, marketing investments, slotting fees), and vendor onboarding workflows. Assortment Merchandising Strategy: Digital shelf optimization, hyper-local assortment planning, regional taste mapping, A/B testing on product placement, and tail-end SKU rationalization. 3. Facilitation, Onboarding Bootcamps Coaching Design and lead high-touch onboarding bootcamps for new category team members to ensure functional readiness within their first 30 to 60 days. Establish and run "Train-the-Trainer" (TTT) programs to equip Category Directors and Senior CMs to act as internal faculty, mentors, and subject-matter experts (SMEs). Facilitate interactive workshops, real-play negotiation clinics, and post-campaign review sessions analyzing previous commercial performance data. 4. Learning Analytics Business Impact Assessment Deploy Kirkpatrick s 4-Level Evaluation Model (Reaction, Learning, Behavior, and Results) to continuously monitor program effectiveness. Maintain data-driven LD dashboards tracking key performance indicators such as program completion rates, assessment scores, ramp-up time, and business-level impacts (e.g., improved margin outcomes in negotiations). Execute periodic refresher assessments and cohort-level gap analyses to ensure learning content remains updated in response to evolving market dynamics. Qualifications Requirements Educational Background: Bachelor s or Master s degree in Business Administration (MBA), Human Resource Development, Organizational Psychology, or a related discipline. Professional Experience: 4 to 8 years of proven experience in Learning Development, Capability Building, or Functional Training, with significant exposure to E-Commerce, Quick-Commerce, Retail, FMCG, or Strategy/Management Consulting. Functional Domain Knowledge: Deep practical understanding of retail merchandising, category management processes, vendor negotiations, assortment strategies, and financial metrics (PL, COGS, Gross Margin). Instructional Methodology: Mastery of adult learning principles, instructional design models (ADDIE, SAM), blended learning architecture, and performance-support tool creation. Analytical Technical Proficiency: Strong ability to interpret business metrics using Excel and BI reporting tools to measure learning impact and business correlations. Stakeholder Management: Proven track record of building trust and driving alignment with senior executives, functional leaders, cross-functional partners (Product, Supply Chain, Revenue), and external training solution providers. Key Performance Metrics for the Role Onboarding Ramp-Up Time: Reduction in Time-to-Productivity (TTP) for newly onboarded Category Managers and ACMs from day of joining to independent capability. Program Engagement Completion: High completion rates and strong satisfaction scores (CSAT/NPS) across cohort training modules and workshops. Capability Shift Business Outcomes: Measurable improvements in functional pre/post-assessment scores and correlation with business metrics (e.g., negotiation success rates, margin improvements, stockout reduction). Playbook Adoption: Active utilization and adoption rate of standardized category playbooks and reference frameworks across all Instamart category verticals.

title: Head Talent Management And Development
description:
The GM / Director Enterprise Performance & Talent Management will act as the operating and design partner to the VP leadingenterprise Performance and Talent Management charter.
The role will translate Sports Team with Heart into a simpler, always-on system that improves performance clarity, talent differentiation, succession, leadership movement and timely action on underperformance.
The core mandate is to build and institutionalise enterprise PMTM architecture and operating engine—strengthening performance, talent density, succession, leadership acceleration and underperformance management through data, technology and AI.
 Key Accountabilities 
1. Transform Performance Management
 Redesign the annual and mid-year performance model into a low-bureaucracy, year-round performance rhythm. Retain a high-performance bar while enabling clear and meaningful differentiation. Create simple role scorecards, regular check-ins and concise performance evidence. Separate ongoing performance conversations from the annual reward-decision window. Establish practical standards for strong performance, exceptional impact and sustained underperformance. Improve performance clarity and reduce year-end surprises. 2. Lead Enterprise Talent and Succession Processes Own the architecture and end-to-end execution of AVP+ talent reviews, critical-role succession, talent risk, internal movement and Founders Club. Prepare high-quality talent-review inputs, decision packs, scenarios and recommendations for the VP and senior leadership forums. Translate every talent review into clear actions: accelerate, move, build, secure, redeploy or transition. Track action closure and proactively surface slippages, talent risks and successor gaps. Strengthen the connection between talent reviews, differentiated deployment and enterprise impact. 3. Build the PMTM Operating Engine Create an integrated operating model across HRBPs, Rewards, L&D, DEI,People Analytics, HR Technology and Employee Relations. Own the PMTM roadmap, governance, policy integration, process calendar and programme discipline. Define decision rights, standards, milestones, ownership and escalation mechanisms. Ensure consistent enterprise standards while allowing for relevant business context. Build and develop a capable team that can independently run the charter day to day. Institutionalise disciplined execution and closure across all PMTM programmes. 4. Use AI, Data and Technology to Simplify PMTM
 Make AI-enabled simplification a core design principle, with human judgment and managerial accountability remaining non-negotiable. Identify and implement practical use cases such as: Goal-quality checks Evidence consolidation Check-in summaries Manager nudges Talent-review packs Performance-pattern analysis Succession-risk identification Talent-movement insights Underperformance signals Reduce forms, manual follow-ups and repetitive reporting. Improve manager and employee experience through simpler, faster workflows. Establish appropriate privacy, fairness, bias and human-in-the-loop controls for AI-enabled workflows. 5. Strengthen Manager Execution and Adoption Ensure the PMTM system changes manager behaviour rather than becoming another HR process. Partner with L&D to build manager capability in: Goal clarity
 Ongoing feedback
 Performance differentiation
 Talent conversations
 Difficult performance discussions
 Run pilots, gather user feedback and iterate before enterprise scale-up. Measure quality of adoption and decision outcomes, not only process completion. Build adoption across businesses with different operating models, leadership styles and maturity levels. 6. Provide Decision Support to the VP and Senior Forums
 Enable high-quality executive talent decisions through rigorous preparation, synthesis and follow-through. Develop concise, fact-based briefs, scenario options and recommendations for sensitive talent and succession discussions. Pre-wire data, process and implementation considerations with HR and business stakeholders. Support CEO, CHRO and CXO forums with accurate, confidential and decision-ready information. Maintain disciplined follow-through and closure after senior leadership forums. Role Boundaries 
 VP – HRBP & Enterprise PMTM Owns 
 Enterprise PMTM philosophy and final design choices
 Challenge, final judgment and closure with CXOs on senior talent decisions
 Executive sponsorship and alignment with the CEO and CHRO
 GM / Director – Enterprise Performance & Talent Management Owns 
 PMTM design, programme leadership and end-to-end execution
 Decision preparation, insight synthesis and recommendations
 Cross-functional integration and technology enablement
 Programme governance, implementation discipline and action closure
 Day-to-day leadership of the PMTM operating engine and team
 Expected Outcomes in the First 12 Months 
 A future-ready PMTM architecture with clear governance, decision rights and an implementation roadmap.
 Material reduction in appraisal-cycle duration, forms, manual follow-ups and manager/HR effort.
 A year-round performance rhythm with clearer expectations, stronger differentiation and fewer year-end surprises.
 High-quality AVP+ talent reviews with improved succession visibility and disciplined action closure.
 A sharper Founders Club linked to differentiated deployment and enterprise impact.
 AI-enabled workflows that improve speed, insight quality and user experience.
 Earlier resolution of persistent underperformance through stronger manager capability and clearer standards.
 A capable PMTM team operating with increasing independence and consistency.
 Candidate Profile 
 Experience 
 12–17 years of progressive HR experience.
 Meaningful ownership of performance management, talent management, succession, organisation development or enterprise HR transformation.
 Experience designing and implementing enterprise-wide people processes.
 Business Grounding 
 Strong HRBP or business-facing experience.
 Ability to understand operating complexity, role scale and business context.
 Clear understanding of the difference between visibility, activity and sustained impact.
 Design and Execution 
 Demonstrated experience redesigning or materially improving enterprise people processes.
 Ability to build the governance, team and operating discipline needed to execute at scale.
 Strong programme-management capability across complex, cross-functional initiatives.
 Talent Judgement 
 Ability to synthesise performance, potential, behaviour and role-fit evidence.
 Strong judgement in developing clear options and recommendations for senior decision-makers.
 Experience handling sensitive talent, succession and underperformance matters with discretion.
 Digital Orientation 
 Hands-on understanding of HR technology, analytics and practical AI use cases.
 Ability to translate data and AI capabilities into usable PMTM workflows and manager experiences.
 Understanding of privacy, fairness, bias and human-in-the-loop controls.
 Leadership Style 
 Low ego and high ownership.
 Calm under pressure and comfortable with ambiguity.
 Highly confidential and trustworthy.
 Collaborative, structured and capable of operating with pace.
 Able to drive daily follow-through without requiring constant direction from the VP.
 Critical Capabilities 
 Enterprise PMTM architecture
 Performance and talent process design
 Succession and talent-risk management
 Simplification and employee experience
 Enterprise programme leadership
 Executive decision support
 AI and data fluency
 Manager enablement and change adoption
 Cross-functional stakeholder management
 Underperformance management and performance differentiation
 Success Measures 
Success in this role will be measured through:
 Reduction in appraisal-cycle duration and administrative effort.
 Quality and timeliness of PMTM programme delivery.
 Timely closure of talent-review and succession actions.
 Improved succession visibility for critical roles.
 Fewer year-end performance surprises.
 Faster and more consistent resolution of persistent underperformance.
 Improved movement and retention of identified high-impact talent.
 Adoption, usability and effectiveness of AI-enabled PMTM workflows and insights.
 Increasing independence and effectiveness of the PMTM team.

title: Cluster Assistant Human Resource Manager
description:
Cluster Assistant Human Resource Manager Brand: Holiday Inn Express - IHG Hotels Resorts 
 Department: Human Resources 
 Job Band: 06 
 Location: Cluster Role - Hyderabad, Bengaluru Chennai, India 
 Reports To: Portfolio HR Director 
 Travel Requirement: Frequent inter-property travel across assigned hotels About Holiday Inn Express At Holiday Inn Express, we believe in making travel simple and smart. We focus on delivering a comfortable stay, friendly service and the essentials that matter most to our guests. As part of IHG Hotels Resorts, we are committed to creating True Hospitality for everyone. We are looking for a people-oriented HR professional who can support our hotel teams, strengthen employee engagement and drive consistent HR practices across our multi-property portfolio. Role Overview - What Is the Job The Cluster Assistant HR Manager will support and drive the Human Resources function across assigned Holiday Inn Express hotels in Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai. The role will be responsible for implementing HR policies and procedures, talent acquisition, employee engagement, learning and development, performance management, employee relations, payroll coordination and statutory compliance. The position will work closely with General Managers, Hotel Managers, Department Heads and the Portfolio HR Director to build a positive workplace culture, ensure compliance with applicable employment laws and support business performance through effective people management. This is a multi-property role requiring strong execution, stakeholder management, analytical skills and the ability to travel regularly across assigned hotel locations. Key Responsibilities 1. Human Resources Operations Manage and coordinate day-to-day HR operations across assigned hotel properties, ensuring consistency in HR processes and adherence to company policies. Maintain accurate employee records, personnel files, HR documentation, attendance and employee lifecycle data. Coordinate onboarding, induction, confirmation, transfers, promotions, employee separations and full-and-final settlement inputs. Support the implementation and effective utilisation of HRMS and recruitment systems. Ensure timely preparation of HR reports, manpower updates, organisational structures and other management reports. Maintain confidentiality and accuracy of employee information and HR records. 2. Talent Acquisition and Manpower Planning Coordinate end-to-end recruitment activities, including manpower requisitions, candidate sourcing, interview scheduling, selection coordination and offer management. Partner with General Managers and Department Heads to understand manpower requirements and ensure timely recruitment. Monitor vacancies, recruitment turnaround time, joining ratios and manpower availability across the assigned hotels. Ensure recruitment practices comply with IHG standards, company policies and applicable employment requirements. Support effective manpower planning, internal career progression and talent development initiatives. 3. Payroll, Compensation Benefits Coordinate monthly attendance, payroll inputs, employee master updates, leave data, incentives and other salary-related information with the respective stakeholders and payroll team. Review payroll inputs for completeness and accuracy and facilitate timely resolution of discrepancies. Coordinate employee benefits, salary revisions, reimbursements and other compensation-related processes as applicable. Monitor employee costs and manpower expenses against approved budgets. Support preparation and validation of payroll reports, employee cost analysis and related management information. 4. Statutory Compliance and Employee Documentation Ensure timely coordination and monitoring of applicable statutory compliances, including EPF, ESIC, Professional Tax, Labour Welfare Fund, minimum wages, bonus, gratuity and other applicable employment requirements. Coordinate with payroll teams, external consultants, vendors and relevant stakeholders for statutory calculations, payments, returns, registers and documentation. Monitor applicable central and state employment laws, statutory deadlines, regulatory changes and establishment-specific requirements. Maintain compliance records, licences, registers, notices and other prescribed documentation as applicable. Conduct periodic HR compliance reviews and support internal and external audits. Track compliance gaps, facilitate corrective actions and escalate material risks to the Portfolio HR Director and relevant management. 5. Employee Engagement, Relations Retention Promote the IHG Winning Ways culture and create a positive, inclusive and engaging work environment. Plan and coordinate employee engagement activities, recognition programmes, celebrations and team-building initiatives. Support employee satisfaction surveys and develop action plans based on feedback. Address employee queries, grievances and workplace concerns promptly, fairly and confidentially. Conduct exit interviews, analyse attrition and absenteeism trends, and recommend appropriate retention initiatives. Build effective relationships with employees, Department Heads and hotel leadership teams. 6. Learning, Development Performance Management Coordinate new-joiner induction, HR orientation and employee awareness programmes. Support training needs identification and the implementation of learning and development initiatives. Guide managers on HR policies, performance management, employee development and people-related matters. Monitor performance appraisal cycles, probation reviews and confirmation processes. Support succession planning, talent development and internal career opportunities. Encourage continuous learning and reinforce the service culture expected at Holiday Inn Express. 7. Employee Welfare, POSH Workplace Standards Support implementation of employee welfare initiatives and workplace policies. Coordinate awareness programmes relating to the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) and other applicable workplace requirements. Support the appropriate handling and escalation of workplace complaints in accordance with company policy and applicable law. Promote respectful workplace behaviour, equal opportunity and a culture of inclusion. Ensure employee-related departmental SOPs and HR standards are communicated and followed. 8. Business Partnership Guest Experience Partner with General Managers and Department Heads to align HR initiatives with hotel business objectives and guest service standards. Support service standards audits and communicate relevant people-related observations and improvement opportunities. Develop initiatives to motivate employees and improve service delivery, productivity and guest satisfaction. Monitor staffing levels, employee productivity and labour costs to support operational efficiency. Contribute to regional and portfolio-level HR initiatives, projects and special assignments as directed by the Portfolio HR Director. 9. HR Reporting, Analytics Continuous Improvement Prepare periodic HR dashboards and reports covering manpower, vacancies, attrition, absenteeism, employee movements, payroll costs and other key HR metrics. Analyse workforce trends and provide actionable insights to hotel leadership. Maintain accurate and timely HR data across all assigned properties. Identify opportunities to simplify HR processes, improve employee experience and strengthen operational controls. Ensure timely completion of assigned deliverables, management reports and compliance trackers. Qualifications Experience Graduate degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Hotel Management or a related discipline. Approximately 3-4 years of relevant Human Resources experience, preferably in the hospitality industry or a multi-property environment. Working knowledge of recruitment, payroll coordination, employee relations, HR operations and statutory compliance. Understanding of applicable Indian labour laws and employment regulations. Experience working with HRMS, recruitment systems, Microsoft Excel and HR reporting tools. Strong communication, coordination, problem-solving and stakeholder-management skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities and travel frequently across assigned hotel locations. Key Skills Competencies Multi-property HR operations and execution. Talent acquisition and manpower planning. Payroll coordination and statutory compliance. Employee engagement and grievance handling. HR analytics, reporting and Excel proficiency. Communication, collaboration and influencing skills. Confidentiality, integrity and attention to detail. Ability to work independently while collaborating with hotel leadership teams. A service-oriented mindset and commitment to continuous improvement. How Will You Deliver Success At IHG, our commitment to True Hospitality is reflected in how we work and how we treat people. True Attitude: Demonstrate care, respect and a genuine desire to make a positive difference. True Confidence: Apply HR knowledge and professional judgement to support employees and business leaders. True Listening: Understand employee and stakeholder concerns and respond with empathy and professionalism. True Responsiveness: Resolve queries efficiently, meet deadlines and take ownership of commitments. Success in this role will be reflected in consistent HR execution across assigned properties, timely recruitment and payroll coordination, strong employee engagement, reliable compliance management and effective partnership with hotel leadership. What We Offer The opportunity to work with the globally recognised IHG Hotels Resorts brand. Exposure to multi-property HR operations and business partnering. Opportunities for professional learning, development and career growth. A collaborative and inclusive working environment. Access to applicable IHG employee benefits, training and development programmes, subject to company policy. Equal Opportunity Employer IHG Hotels Resorts is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace where colleagues are respected, valued and encouraged to contribute their best. title: Sr Manager - HR Business Partner
description:
About us 
 Scimplify is a science-first manufacturing company for Advanced Materials: from specialty chemicals to the emerging building blocks of next-generation energy applications, life sciences, and crop sciences. We scale process development and manufacturing as one continuous system, supported by world-class R&D infrastructure and executed across a global network of 500+ manufacturing partners and thousands of scientists and technical partners. The result: new materials go from molecule to commercial scale in months, not years. Scimplify operates offices and teams across 5 countries with 1,000+ innovator customers in 40+ countries. We are backed by investors such as Accel, Bertelsmann, Omnivore, Hitachi Ventures and 3one4 Capital, having raised over $80M. 
 Role overview 
 We are looking for a Senior HR Business Partner (HRBP) to work closely with the Founders and senior leadership in building and strengthening Scimplifys people practices, HR processes, policies, and organizational capabilities. This is a strategic yet hands-on role for an HR professional who understands how a business operates and can translate business priorities into effective people practices. The individual will partner with the Founders to understand the business in depth, identify organizational and people-related challenges, and build scalable HR frameworks that support business growth. The role will have significant ownership in establishing SOPs, designing and implementing HR policies, strengthening organizational effectiveness, and partnering with business leaders on workforce planning, performance management, leadership development, employee relations, and talent retention. We are looking for someone who has previously built and implemented HR processes and policies from the ground up , ideally in a high-growth startup or evolving business environment, and can operate with ownership, sound judgment, and minimal supervision. 
 Key responsibilities 1. Strategic Business Partnering Work closely with the Founders and business leaders to understand Scimplifys business model, growth plans, operating structure, and organizational priorities. Develop a deep understanding of business functions, their operational challenges, talent requirements, and people-related risks. Partner with business leaders to translate business objectives into people strategies and actionable HR initiatives. Provide data-driven insights and recommendations on organizational effectiveness, workforce productivity, employee retention, and leadership effectiveness. Act as a trusted advisor to leadership on people decisions, organizational design, team structures, and workforce planning. Proactively identify people-related challenges and develop practical solutions aligned with business priorities. 2. HR Process & Policy Development Build, review, and implement HR policies, SOPs, guidelines, and frameworks aligned with Scimplifys evolving business requirements. Establish standardized HR processes across the employee lifecycle, ensuring consistency, clarity, and accountability. Identify gaps in existing HR practices and introduce scalable processes to support organizational growth. Develop clear policy documentation, process workflows, approval matrices, and governance mechanisms. Ensure policies are practical, business-friendly, and consistently implemented across teams and locations. Periodically review policies and processes to improve efficiency, employee experience, and compliance. 3. Organization Design & Workforce Planning Partner with Founders and business leaders on organization structure, role clarity, reporting relationships, and manpower planning. Support headcount planning, workforce budgeting, resource allocation, and organizational capability assessment. Identify skill gaps, critical roles, succession requirements, and opportunities to improve team effectiveness. Help build scalable organizational structures as the business expands into new functions, markets, and geographies. 4. Performance Management & Talent Development Design and strengthen performance management frameworks, including goal setting, KPIs, performance reviews, and feedback mechanisms. Work with leaders to improve performance accountability and establish a high-performance culture. Identify high-potential employees and critical talent; develop retention and career progression strategies. Support leadership development, manager capability building, and succession planning. Partner with business leaders to address performance gaps and make informed talent decisions. 5. Employee Relations & Culture Serve as a trusted point of contact for employees and managers on workplace matters, employee concerns, and organizational challenges. Establish structured mechanisms for employee feedback, grievance resolution, and conflict management. Help build a culture of ownership, accountability, transparency, and collaboration. Drive initiatives to strengthen employee engagement, manager effectiveness, and retention. Support change management initiatives and help teams navigate organizational growth and evolving ways of working. 6. HR Operations, Governance & Compliance Work closely with HR and relevant business teams to strengthen onboarding, employee documentation, exit management, HR systems, and employee lifecycle processes. Establish HR dashboards and people analytics to track headcount, attrition, performance, workforce costs, and other critical metrics. Ensure HR policies and practices align with applicable employment laws and statutory requirements, in partnership with relevant specialists where needed. Establish appropriate governance, documentation, and approval mechanisms for key people processes. Drive continuous improvement and ensure HR processes remain efficient, auditable, and scalable. 7. Founder & Leadership Partnership Work directly with the Founders on strategic people initiatives and organization-wide HR priorities. Challenge existing practices constructively and recommend solutions that balance business needs, employee experience, and organizational effectiveness. Independently drive HR projects from problem identification through design, implementation, and adoption. Provide regular updates to leadership on people priorities, policy implementation, organizational risks, and progress against agreed initiatives. Desired candidate profile MBA / PGDM in Human Resources or a relevant postgraduate qualification. Approximately 10-15 years of HR experience, with substantial experience in HR business partnering and organizational development. Currently working in an HRBP, Senior HRBP, Lead HRBP, or equivalent role with meaningful ownership of business partnering and HR process development. Demonstrated experience building and implementing HR policies, SOPs, and frameworks, preferably in a startup, scale-up, or rapidly evolving organization. Strong experience partnering directly with Founders, CXOs, business heads, or senior leadership. A proven ability to understand business models, operating challenges, and commercial priorities and translate them into effective people practices. Experience in performance management, organization design, workforce planning, employee relations, talent management, and change management. Strong stakeholder management, communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently, navigate ambiguity, influence senior stakeholders, and drive execution without relying on established processes. A balance of strategic thinking and hands-on implementation.

description:
Job Summary 
 Job Title: Maintenance Assistant Department: Maintenance Reporting to: Assistant Manager Projects Maintenance 

 Responsibilities 
 Assemble, install, test, and maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus, and fixtures, using hand tools and power tools. Diagnose malfunctioning systems, apparatus, and components, using test equipment and hand tools, to locate the cause of a breakdown and correct the problem. Connect wires to circuit breakers, transformers, or other components. Inspect electrical systems, equipment, and components to identify hazards, defects, and the need for adjustment or repair, and to ensure compliance with codes. Advise management on whether continued operation of equipment could be hazardous. Test electrical systems and continuity of circuits in electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures, using testing devices such as ohmmeters, voltmeters, and oscilloscopes, to ensure compatibility and safety of system. Maintain current electricians license or identification card to meet governmental regulations. Plan layout and installation of electrical wiring, equipment and fixtures, based on job specifications and local codes. Direct and train workers to install, maintain, or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures. Prepare sketches or follow blueprints to determine the location of wiring and equipment and to ensure conformance to building and safety codes. Use a variety of tools and equipment such as power construction equipment, measuring devices, power tools, and testing equipment including oscilloscopes, ammeters, and test lamps. Install ground leads and connect power cables to equipment, such as motors. Perform business management duties such as maintaining records and files, preparing reports and ordering supplies and equipment. Repair or replace wiring, equipment, and fixtures, using hand tools and power tools. Work from ladders, scaffolds, and roofs to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures. Place conduit (pipes or tubing) inside designated partitions, walls, or other concealed areas, and pull insulated wires or cables through the conduit to complete circuits between boxes. Construct and fabricate parts, using hand tools and specifications. Fasten small metal or plastic boxes to walls to house electrical switches or outlets. Perform physically demanding tasks, such as digging trenches to lay conduit and moving and lifting heavy objects. Provide preliminary sketches and cost estimates for materials and services. Provide assistance during emergencies by operating floodlights and generators, placing flares, and driving needed vehicles.

 Result Oriented Knowledge of Business Customer Focus Teamwork Adaptability Communication skills Problem Solving and Decision making

 Reporting To: HR Manager / Factory Head 
 1. Job Purpose To manage and strengthen employee welfare activities at the garment manufacturing facility, ensuring a safe, supportive, compliant, and employee-friendly workplace, with particular focus on the needs of women employees. The role will be responsible for employee welfare facilities, grievance handling, statutory welfare requirements, employee engagement, counselling/support, and coordination with internal departments and external agencies. 
 2. Key Responsibilities A. Absenteeism, Attrition & Employee Retention Management Monitor and analyse daily, weekly, and monthly absenteeism and attrition trends. Identify root causes of absenteeism and employee turnover through employee interactions, feedback, stay interviews and exit interviews. Track department-wise, line-wise, shift-wise and tenure-wise absenteeism and attrition. Identify high-risk employees and groups and take proactive retention measures. Follow up with frequent/long-absent employees and understand their concerns to support their return to work. Conduct regular employee connect sessions to identify and resolve workplace and welfare-related concerns. Develop and implement employee engagement and retention initiatives, particularly for women employees. Coordinate with HR, Production, and supervisors to address issues related to work environment, supervisors, transport, canteen, accommodation, working hours, and other welfare concerns. Monitor early attrition, particularly employee exits within the first 30/60/90 days, and recommend corrective actions. Prepare regular absenteeism, attrition, and retention MIS reports and present key findings and action plans to management. Measure the effectiveness of retention initiatives and continuously recommend improvements to reduce absenteeism and attrition. 
 B. Employee Welfare & Facilities Manage day-to-day employee welfare activities within the factory. Ensure availability and proper maintenance of welfare facilities such as: Canteen Drinking water Rest areas Washrooms Changing rooms First-aid facilities Transport facilities Childcare/crche facilities, where applicable Conduct regular welfare-facility inspections and coordinate corrective actions. Ensure welfare facilities are clean, hygienic, safe and accessible to employees. 
 C. Women Employee Welfare Act as a key point of contact for women employees regarding welfare-related concerns. Handle women employees' grievances with sensitivity and confidentiality. Support awareness initiatives related to workplace safety, dignity and respectful behaviour. Coordinate with relevant committees and management on matters concerning women employees. Support implementation and awareness of the organisation's POSH policy and related processes. Monitor issues affecting women employees and escalate serious concerns to HR management. 
 D. Employee Grievance Handling Receive, understand, and document employee grievances. Conduct employee interaction sessions and floor-level feedback activities. Coordinate with HR, Production, Compliance, and other departments to resolve grievances. Maintain proper records of grievances and closure status. Identify recurring employee issues and recommend preventive actions. 
 E. Statutory & Social Compliance Support HR/Compliance teams in meeting applicable labour and welfare requirements. Maintain welfare-related records and documentation required for audits and inspections. Coordinate preparation for customer/social-compliance audits. Ensure welfare practices are implemented in line with company policies and applicable statutory requirements. Support inspections by government authorities and other external agencies when required. 
 F. Employee Engagement Plan and coordinate employee engagement and welfare activities. Organise events and programmes such as:
 Employee awareness programmes Health and wellness activities Women's Day programmes Sports and cultural activities Employee recognition programmes Festival celebrations Counselling / awareness sessions Promote positive employee relations and improve employee participation. 
 G. Communication & Awareness Conduct regular employee awareness sessions on welfare-related topics. Communicate HR and welfare initiatives effectively to employees. Coordinate toolbox talks, awareness campaigns, and employee meetings. Ensure employees understand available welfare facilities and support systems. 
 H. Employee Support & Counselling Maintain regular interaction with employees at the shop-floor level. Identify employee concerns relating to work environment, accommodation, transport, canteen, health, safety or personal difficulties. Provide basic counselling/support within the scope of the role and escalate sensitive or serious matters appropriately. Maintain confidentiality of employee information. 
 I. Reporting & Documentation Prepare periodic welfare reports for management. Track welfare complaints, actions and closure. Maintain records of welfare activities, inspections, meetings and employee engagement programmes. Analyse employee feedback and recommend improvements. Provide MIS reports to the HR Manager / Factory Head as required. 
 3. Key Skills & Competencies Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Good employee-handling and grievance-management skills. Empathy and patience when dealing with employees. Strong understanding of workplace welfare practices. Ability to communicate effectively with women employees and shop-floor workers. Good coordination and problem-solving skills. Ability to maintain confidentiality. Good documentation and reporting skills. Ability to work independently as well as coordinate with cross-functional teams. Basic knowledge of MS Office / Excel / HR systems. 
 4. Qualification Master's degree in HR, Social Work, Labour Welfare, MBA or related discipline. 
 5. Experience 6-10 years of relevant experience in employee welfare / HR/labour welfare, preferably in the garment, textile, manufacturing or factory environment . Experience handling a predominantly female workforce will be an advantage. Experience in social-compliance audits and employee grievance handling is preferred. 
 6. Preferred Knowledge Employee welfare practices Labour welfare requirements Grievance handling Women employee welfare POSH awareness and process coordination Social compliance requirements Factory welfare facilities Employee engagement Basic HR documentation and MIS Audit preparation and documentation 
 7. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Timely closure of employee grievances. Employee satisfaction with welfare facilities. Welfare facility inspection and corrective-action closure. Employee engagement and participation levels. Compliance with welfare-related requirements. Audit observations and timely closure. Effectiveness of employee communication and awareness programmes. Reduction in recurring employee welfare complaints.

title: Head of HR
description:
Head of HR Human Resources 
 Job Summary We are looking for an experienced Head of HR to lead the overall human resources function for a growing, mid-sized organisation. The role will partner closely with the CEO and senior leadership team to develop and execute people strategies, strengthen organisational culture, build leadership capabilities, and establish scalable HR processes. 
 The ideal candidate will have strong experience across strategic HR business partnering, talent acquisition, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee engagement, HR operations, and statutory compliance. The candidate should be commercially oriented, comfortable advising senior leadership, and capable of building a high-performing HR function that supports business growth. 
 Key Responsibilities 1. Strategic HR & Business Partnering Develop and implement a comprehensive HR strategy aligned with organisational goals. Partner with the CEO and leadership team on workforce planning, organisation design, restructuring, and change management. Develop people strategies that improve productivity, engagement, retention, and organisational effectiveness. Present HR metrics, workforce insights, and recommendations to senior management. 2. Talent Acquisition & Employer Branding Lead recruitment strategy across leadership, managerial, and critical business positions. Build scalable recruitment processes, structured interviews, and candidate assessment frameworks. Improve time-to-hire, quality-of-hire, offer acceptance, and employee retention. Strengthen employer branding and talent sourcing strategies. 3. Performance Management & Compensation Design and manage performance appraisal systems, goal setting, feedback, and performance calibration. Develop compensation structures, salary bands, grading frameworks, and variable-pay policies. Establish career progression, internal mobility, and succession planning frameworks. Support leadership hiring, assessment, and long-term incentive initiatives where applicable. 4. Learning, Development & Employee Engagement Develop leadership development and management capability programs. Identify skill gaps and implement employee learning initiatives. Drive employee engagement, culture-building, recognition, and retention programs. Monitor engagement feedback and implement measurable improvement initiatives. 5. HR Operations & Statutory Compliance Oversee HR operations, onboarding, payroll coordination, employee exits, HR policies, and employee records. Ensure compliance with applicable Indian employment and labour laws, including PF, ESI, gratuity, POSH, and relevant state-specific requirements. Manage employee relations, grievance resolution, investigations, and disciplinary processes. Strengthen HR systems, documentation, internal controls, and compliance audits. Implement HR analytics to track attrition, headcount, recruitment efficiency, and workforce costs. 6. Team Leadership Lead and develop HR business partners, talent acquisition, HR operations, and learning and development teams. Establish clear accountability, performance standards, and operating processes within HR. Build a high-performing HR function capable of supporting organisational expansion. 
 Required Qualifications & Experience 14-20 years of progressive HR experience, including at least 5 years in a Head of HR, HR Director, or senior HR Business Partner role. Experience supporting or leading HR in an organisation with approximately 3002,000 employees. Strong understanding of strategic HR, talent acquisition, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee engagement, and HR operations. Demonstrated experience in workforce planning, organisational development, change management, and leadership advisory. Strong knowledge of Indian labour laws and statutory compliance requirements. Experience managing and developing HR teams. Excellent stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and decision-making skills. MBA/PGDM in HR, MHRM, or an equivalent relevant qualification preferred. 
 Preferred Experience Experience in IT services, technology, BFSI, professional services, or other growth-oriented organisations. Experience in founder-led, high-growth, or PE/VC-backed businesses. Exposure to HRIS implementation, HR analytics, compensation benchmarking, and leadership hiring. Experience designing succession planning and long-term incentive frameworks. 
 Key Competencies Strategic HR Leadership | Business Partnering | Talent Acquisition | Compensation & Benefits | Performance Management | Employee Relations | Labour Law Compliance | Organisational Development | Change Management | HR Analytics | Leadership Development 
 What We Offer Opportunity to shape the organisation's people strategy. Direct engagement with the CEO and senior leadership team. Competitive compensation and performance-linked incentives. Scope to modernise HR processes and build a scalable people function.

 Service Reports Installation Reports Customer Feedback Forms Vouchers Other relevant service documents Coordinate with service engineers to ensure proper documentation and timely submission.

Maintain professional communication and ensure timely follow-up on customer requirements. Coordinate for acknowledgement of spare parts/materials delivered through service engineers. 
 5. Spares & Gate Entry Coordination

Coordinate and collect required documentation such as delivery reports and gate entry details . Ensure proper records are maintained and submitted to the concerned department/head office. 
 6. Branch Administration

Coordinate housekeeping activities and ensure cleanliness and proper upkeep of the office/store area. Handle submission and coordination of various office utility bills and administrative documents with the Head Office. Maintain required attendance and administrative records of in-house staff. 
 7. Petty Cash & Courier Management 
 Handle branch-level petty cash and maintain proper records, supporting documents, and vouchers. Coordinate all incoming and outgoing courier activities. Maintain courier records and ensure timely dispatch and receipt of documents/materials. 
 8. Call Handling & Communication 
 Attend incoming and outgoing calls professionally. Direct calls to the concerned person, department, or extension. Maintain required call/communication records. Coordinate internal and external communication as required for smooth branch operations. 
 9. Inventory & Stock Coordination 
 Maintain proper stock records for the branch/store. Monitor stock movement and ensure records are updated regularly. Coordinate with the Stores Department regarding stock availability, movement, and requirements. Ensure proper documentation of material movement. Candidate Profile Must-have experience: 4–8 years of experience in HR Employee Relations / HR Legal / Labour Relations / Industrial Relations . Hands-on experience handling employee disputes and disciplinary cases . Experience dealing with absconding, notice-period recovery, termination and separation-related cases . Exposure to Labour Courts / Labour Commissioner / labour authorities and coordination with external lawyers. Good understanding of Indian Labour & Employment Laws. Strong drafting, documentation and communication skills. Preferred: LLB / LLM qualification. Experience in a large employee-base organisation, preferably Retail, F&B, Hospitality, FMCG, Manufacturing or other multi-location businesses .  Senior Design Verification Engineer - Silicon Engineering / 3-10 Years Job Description 
 Job Description Senior Design Verification Engineer Experience: 310 Years Location: Bangalore / Ahmedabad / Pune / Hyderabad Job Overview 
 We are seeking an experienced and highly skilled Senior Design Verification Engineer with 310 years of hands-on experience in Design Verification. As a key member of our team, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the robustness and correctness of our cutting-edge System-on-Chip designs. Responsibilities 
 Lead and manage Design Verification efforts for complex projects, ensuring the successful execution of verification plans. Develop and implement comprehensive verification strategies, test plans, and test benches for high-speed SoCs, including low-speed peripherals like I2c/i3c, SPI, UART, GPIO, QSPI , and high-speed protocols like PCIe, Ethernet, CXL, MIPI, DDR, and HBM . Conduct Gate-level simulations and power-aware verification using Xprop and UPF . Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, architects, designers, and pre/post-silicon verification teams. Analyze and implement SystemVerilog assertions and coverage ( code, toggle, functional ). Provide mentorship and technical guidance to junior verification engineers. Manage and lead a dynamic team of verification engineers, fostering a collaborative and innovative work environment. Ensure verification signoff criteria are met and documentation is comprehensive. Demonstrate dedication, hard work, and commitment to achieving project goals and deadlines. Adhere to quality standards, implement good test practices, and contribute to the continuous improvement of verification methodologies. Experience with verification tools from Synopsys and Cadence , including VCS and Xsim . Integration of third-party VIPs (Verification IP) from Synopsys and Cadence. 

 Qualifications 
 Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, or a related field. OR Masters degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, or a related field. OR PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, or a related field. 310 years of hands-on experience in SoC Design Verification. Expertise in UVM (Universal Verification Methodology) and SystemVerilog . Prior experience working on IP-level and SoC-level verification projects. Proficient in verification tools such as VCS, Xsim, waveform analyzers , and third-party VIP integration (e.g., Synopsys VIPs and Cadence VIPs). Hands-on experience with UFS (Universal Flash Storage), Ethernet, PCIe, CXL, and MIPI protocols. Solid understanding of low-speed peripherals ( I2c/i3c, SPI, UART, GPIO, QSPI ) and high-speed protocols. Experience in DDR, HBM, Gate-level simulations , and power-aware verification using Xprop and UPF . Proficiency in scripting languages such as Shell, Makefile, and Perl . Strong understanding of processor-based SoC verification, including Native, Verilog, SystemVerilog, and UVM mixed environments . Experience with C-SystemVerilog handshake and writing C test cases for boot-up verification . Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and debugging skills.

title: HR Manager
description:
We are looking for an experienced and result-oriented HR Manager to manage the complete HR function for an FMCG organization having both corporate office and manufacturing/factory operations. The role will be responsible for the entire employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, payroll, employee engagement, performance management, HR operations, statutory compliance, employee relations, and factory HR activities. HR Operations Manage end-to-end HR operations for corporate office and factory employees. Develop, implement and maintain HR policies, processes and SOPs. Manage employee lifecycle from joining to exit. Maintain employee records and HR documentation. Handle employee queries and provide timely HR support. Monitor attendance, leave, shift schedules and employee movements. Recruitment & Talent Acquisition Manage end-to-end recruitment for corporate, sales, factory and support functions. Understand manpower requirements and prepare recruitment plans. Coordinate with department heads and hiring managers for recruitment. Source candidates through job portals, consultants, referrals and other channels. Conduct/coordinate interviews, salary negotiations and offer rollouts. Ensure timely onboarding of new employees. Payroll & Compensation Manage monthly payroll processing in coordination with Finance/payroll teams. Ensure accurate attendance, leave, overtime, incentives and payroll inputs. Manage salary revisions, increments, deductions and full & final settlements. Handle employee queries related to salary, statutory deductions and benefits. Ensure payroll data is accurate and processed within timelines. Statutory Compliance & Labour Laws Ensure compliance with applicable labour laws and statutory requirements. Manage PF, ESI, PT, Gratuity, Bonus, Minimum Wages, Shops & Establishments Act, Payment of Wages Act and other applicable regulations. Ensure factory-related statutory compliance and labour documentation. Coordinate with statutory consultants, auditors and government authorities. Maintain statutory registers, records, licenses and required documentation. Support labour inspections, audits and statutory assessments. Ensure timely submission/payment of statutory returns and contributions. Factory HR & Employee Relations Manage HR operations at the manufacturing/factory location. Handle manpower planning for production and support functions. Manage contract labour/workmen-related HR activities. Monitor attendance, shifts, overtime, absenteeism and manpower productivity. Handle employee grievances, disciplinary matters and workplace issues. Maintain positive employee relations and a productive work environment. Coordinate with factory management on workforce requirements and HR issues. Support compliance related to Factories Act and applicable state labour regulations. Employee Engagement & Culture Develop and implement employee engagement initiatives. Plan and execute employee events, celebrations and recognition programs. Conduct employee engagement surveys and prepare action plans. Drive employee communication and culture-building initiatives. Manage employee recognition and rewards programs. Improve employee satisfaction, retention and workplace experience. Performance Management Manage the annual performance appraisal process. Coordinate goal setting, KRAs/KPIs and performance reviews. Support managers in performance evaluation and improvement plans. Track probation confirmation and employee performance milestones. Develop initiatives to improve employee productivity and performance. Learning & Development Identify training and development requirements across departments. Prepare and coordinate the annual training calendar. Organize technical, functional, behavioural and compliance training. Evaluate training effectiveness and maintain training records. Support leadership and employee development initiatives. HRMS & HR Analytics Manage and maintain the organization's HRMS. Ensure accurate employee master data and HR records. Manage attendance, leave, recruitment, onboarding and performance modules. Generate HR reports and dashboards for management. Track headcount, attrition, absenteeism, recruitment TAT, manpower cost, overtime and employee engagement metrics. Policies & Process Improvement Develop, review and update HR policies in line with business requirements and applicable laws. Standardize HR processes across corporate and factory locations. Identify opportunities for automation and process improvement. Ensure effective communication and implementation of HR policies. Employee Welfare & Benefits Manage employee welfare initiatives for office and factory employees. Coordinate employee insurance, medical benefits and other welfare schemes. Ensure statutory and company-provided benefits are administered effectively. Address employee concerns related to benefits and welfare. HR MIS & Management Reporting Prepare monthly HR MIS and management dashboards. Provide management with reports on headcount, attrition, recruitment, payroll, absenteeism and manpower cost. Analyze HR trends and recommend corrective actions. Support management in manpower budgeting and workforce planning. Key Skills & Competencies Strong knowledge of HR Operations and HR Generalist functions. Excellent knowledge of Recruitment & Talent Acquisition. Strong Payroll & Compensation knowledge. Good understanding of Labour Laws & Statutory Compliance. Experience in Factory/Manufacturing HR. Employee Relations & Grievance Handling. Employee Engagement & Retention. Performance Management and HR Policy Development. HRMS/HRIS Management and HR Analytics/MIS. Strong communication, stakeholder management, problem-solving and decision-making skills. Ability to manage both white-collar and blue-collar workforce. Educational Qualification MBA / PGDM in Human Resources preferred. Bachelor's degree in any discipline. Relevant HR certifications will be an added advantage. Preferred Experience 7-12 years of HR experience, preferably in FMCG, Manufacturing, Food Processing or a similar industry. Prior experience handling both corporate HR and factory HR is preferred. Experience managing staff, workmen and contract labour will be an advantage. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Recruitment TAT and manpower fulfillment. Employee attrition and retention. Payroll accuracy and timeliness. Statutory compliance and audit performance. Employee engagement score. Absenteeism and overtime management. Training effectiveness. Performance appraisal completion. HR process efficiency and employee grievance resolution TAT. HR cost optimization. Overall Role Objective To build and manage a strong, compliant and employee-focused HR function that supports the company's corporate, sales, warehouse and manufacturing operations, while ensuring effective manpower management, employee engagement, payroll accuracy and statutory compliance

title: Deputy General Manager- HR
description:

Role Purpose To lead and institutionalize the people, organization and workforce agenda across JAPL, JSPL and JMPL, partnering closely with the GM Operation& HR, Business/Plant Heads and functional leadership. The role will be accountable for building a scalable, productive, performance-driven and future-ready organization by strengthening organization design, manpower productivity, talent acquisition, performance management, capability building, succession, employee relations, HR governance and people analytics. The DGM – HR is expected to operate as a business HR leader, moving HR from predominantly transactional support to a function that measurably contributes to business growth, productivity, leadership capability and organizational effectiveness. 2. Key Accountabilities A. Strategic HR Business Partnership Partner with the GM Operation & HR and business leadership to translate business plans into people, organization and capability priorities. Develop annual and 3-year HR plans for JAPL, JSPL and JMPL aligned with growth, capacity, productivity and organizational requirements. Advise leadership on organization structure, manpower, capability, performance, talent and people risks. Build a consistent HR operating model across the three businesses while allowing appropriate business-specific flexibility. Participate in business reviews and ensure people-related actions have clear ownership and closure. B. Organization Design & Manpower Productivity Drive organization structure reviews across businesses/functions. Establish approved manpower norms and budgets linked to production volume, capacity and business plans. 2 Review spans, layers, role clarity and reporting relationships. Drive workforce optimization without compromising safety, quality or delivery. Track manpower productivity, overtime, absenteeism, contract labour utilization and employee cost. Establish clear role charters and accountability across critical positions. Key outcome: Right structure Right manpower Right capability Right cost. C. Talent Acquisition & Workforce Pipeline Own workforce planning and recruitment governance across JAPL, JSPL and JMPL. Ensure timely closure of leadership, managerial, technical and critical shop-floor positions. Build sustainable pipelines through ITI/Diploma institutions, engineering colleges, apprenticeships, trainees, referrals and specialist hiring channels. Strengthen selection quality, onboarding and early-tenure retention. Build succession-oriented internal hiring and career mobility before external recruitment. D. Performance & Accountability Culture Institutionalize a robust Performance Management System across businesses. Ensure goals cascade from: Business Function Department Individual. Strengthen measurable KRAs/KPIs and differentiate performance objectively. Facilitate performance reviews, calibration and consequence management. Link performance with business outcomes such as productivity, quality, delivery, cost, projects, capability and people development. Build stronger managerial accountability for team performance. E. Talent Management, Succession & Leadership Pipeline Identify critical roles and critical talent across all three businesses. Establish succession coverage for key leadership and specialist positions. Conduct structured talent reviews and identify HiPos. Establish Ready Now / Ready in 1–2 Years / Longer-term succession categories. Drive Individual Development Plans for critical talent. Strengthen internal mobility and cross-functional/business exposure. Reduce dependency on individual incumbents and external hiring for key positions. F. Learning, Capability & Skill Architecture Build capability architecture covering operators, technicians, engineers, managers and leadership levels. Establish functional/technical competency matrices. Drive multi-skilling and skill certification for shop-floor workforce. Build structured development journeys for supervisors and managers. 3 Use the 70:20:10 development philosophy for identified leadership talent. Measure training through capability improvement and business impact rather than training hours alone. G. Industrial / Employee Relations & Workforce Governance Maintain a stable, disciplined and productive employee-relations environment across the businesses. Establish robust grievance and disciplinary processes. Ensure appropriate handling of domestic enquiries and employee-relations matters. Govern permanent, trainee, apprentice and contract workforce practices. Partner with operations leadership to proactively address workforce risks. Strengthen employee communication and shop-floor connect mechanisms. H. Statutory Compliance & HR Governance Ensure compliance with applicable labour and employment legislation and factory-related people requirements. Establish compliance calendars and periodic audits across JAPL, JSPL and JMPL. Govern contractor compliance and documentation. Ensure timely closure of audit observations and statutory deviations. Coordinate with legal counsel and government/labour authorities where required. Maintain zero tolerance for material people-related statutory non-compliance. I. Employee Engagement, Culture & Change Build a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration, performance and continuous improvement. Strengthen communication between leadership, managers and employees. Drive structured employee-engagement interventions based on data and business needs. Support organizational transformation, restructuring, digitalization and new ways of working. Build change readiness among managers and employees. Actively identify and address behaviours that impede organizational change. J. HR Operations, Systems & Analytics Standardize critical HR processes across the three businesses. Drive HRMS/digital adoption and improve employee/manager self-service. Establish a monthly HR Business Dashboard for the GM Operation& HR Use workforce analytics for decision-making rather than retrospective reporting. Ensure employee master data, attendance, payroll inputs, lifecycle transactions and documentation are accurate and controlled. 4 3. Employee Relations, Culture & Performance Provide senior oversight and escalation for complex employee relations matters, ensuring issues are resolved fairly, consistently and in line with Indian labour law. Embed performance management practices that build manager capability, support accountability and enable growth across a scaling organisation. Champion employee engagement, inclusion, wellbeing and retention strategies that are meaningful in the Indian talent market and consistent with the company’s global people agenda. 6. Global People Agenda, Policy & Governance Partner with the UK-based Chief People Officer to develop a globally consistent people agenda that supports the company’s growth ambitions while remaining adaptable to local employment contexts. Translate UK head office people strategy, values, governance and cultural expectations into practical India policies, processes and manager guidance. Build policy and governance frameworks that can scale beyond India and support the company’s transition from start-up to global organisation. 7. Leadership Capability, Learning & Organisation Development Identify capability gaps across the Bangalore GCC and develop learning priorities that support business growth, manager effectiveness and future global scale. Work with the UK CPO to develop consistent global leadership expectations, behaviours and people management standards. 8. People Analytics, Reporting & Strategic Insight Ensure HR systems, employee records and reporting processes are accurate, secure, compliant and fit for a growing global business. Develop people dashboards and leadership reporting covering hiring, attrition, engagement, performance, diversity, compliance, capability and organisational risk. Use data and insight to advise the UK CPO and India leadership on strategic people decisions, workforce investment and operational priorities. Establish reporting disciplines that provide visibility across the India GCC and can evolve into a global people reporting framework. 9. Strategic HR Leadership in a Start-Up, GCC and Global Growth Environment Partner with the UK-based Chief People Officer to shape and execute a global people strategy that supports international growth, operational scale and cultural alignment. Act as the senior India people leader, ensuring the Bangalore GCC is integrated into the wider business while remaining responsive to Indian employment law, culture, talent expectations and market dynamics.
